runs.text: The document reports no measurable dissolution of the PVDF binder by ethylene glycol. The authors state that, as confirmed by FTIR and EDX spectra, the PVDF binder was
not removed or dissolved during the EG-based separation process

support.quote: not removed or dissolved during the EG-based separation

runs.text: . They explain this with Hansen solubility parameters: EG has a high HSP distance (Ra) from PVDF, which means a low ability to dissolve PVDF. The delamination is attributed instead to competitive inhibition of the PVDF-current collector bonding through hydrogen bonding, not to dissolution of the binder. So the answer is none: no PVDF dissolution is reported. The document gives no percentage or amount for dissolved binder.

rendered: The document reports no measurable dissolution of the PVDF binder by ethylene glycol. The authors state that, as confirmed by FTIR and EDX spectra, the PVDF binder was not removed or dissolved during the EG-based separation process[1]. They explain this with Hansen solubility parameters: EG has a high HSP distance (Ra) from PVDF, which means a low ability to dissolve PVDF. The delamination is attributed instead to competitive inhibition of the PVDF-current collector bonding through hydrogen bonding, not to dissolution of the binder. So the answer is none: no PVDF dissolution is reported. The document gives no percentage or amount for dissolved binder.
